questions.q: What are the three states of Holt-Winters?
why: Correct: l(t), b(t) and the seasonal values.
These are statistics, not model states.
Error and noise are not states of the method.
There is always a level, and there is no cycle state.

questions.q: Monthly data. How many full seasons do you need at least to start Holt-Winters, and how many values is that?
questions.why: At least two full seasons. Monthly data has m = 12, so 2 * 12 = 24 values.

questions.q: Sales grow, and the Christmas peak is +100 when sales are 1000 but +300 when sales are 3000. Which season type?
why: Correct: the peak is about 10% of the level at both times.
An additive season would be the same +100 at all levels.
There is a clear seasonal peak.
Damped refers to the trend, not the season.

questions.q: Which ETS name is additive Holt-Winters with additive errors?
why: Correct: additive error, additive trend, additive season.
That is simple exponential smoothing.
That has no trend and a multiplicative season and error.
That is the damped trend method without a season.

questions.q: New value 150, old seasonal value +30, alpha = 0.5, old level + trend = 110. What is the new level (additive HW)?
Hourly data has a daily and a weekly pattern. What is the limit of Holt-Winters here?
options: It supports only one season length
It cannot be fitted by least squares
It cannot forecast more than one step
why: Correct: choose one m, or use a model with several seasons.
It needs start values from the first seasons.
Least squares on one-step errors is the usual way.
It forecasts any horizon.

questions.q: Your Holt-Winters model has MAE 12. Seasonal naive has MAE 10. What do you conclude?
options: Holt-Winters is worse than the baseline, so do not ship it as is
Holt-Winters is better because it is more complex
Seasonal naive must have a bug
why: Correct: a model that cannot beat the baseline adds no value. Check the parameters or the season length.
Complexity does not guarantee accuracy.
Both were measured with MAE on the same period, so they are comparable.
Seasonal naive is simple and correct when the pattern repeats.
